RPT.Title: Traps
RPT.NoGM: A GM must be online to set traps.
RPT.DcTip: Item DC {base} · level DC {level} — the setting decides which applies

Pc.Title: Set traps
Pc.Open: Trap-setting is open — set your traps now
Pc.Closed: You can set traps once the GM opens trap-setting
Pc.Secret: Traps set here don't show on the GM's screen
Pc.NoKit: No snares, traps, poisons or caltrops.
Pc.KitHint: DC: the higher of the item's DC and the setter's level DC + {bonus} (configurable), since monsters are usually stronger than the party.
Pc.NonePlaced: None yet. Click 'Set' on the left, then a square on the map.
Pc.PickupHint: Take the trap back into the party's packs
Pc.DoneLine: {name}: the players have set {n} trap(s). (Their locations are secret.)

Gm.Title: Traps — GM
Gm.PhaseOpen: Player trap-setting: open (they're setting traps in secret)
Gm.PeekHint: Show the players' traps on your screen only, for {s} seconds.
Gm.PeekLine: The GM peeked at the trap locations.
Gm.ClearPcHint: Clear every player trap (without looking at them)
Gm.ClearPcAsk: Clear every player trap on this scene? (They don't return to the packs.)
Gm.ClearGmAsk: Clear every GM trap on this scene?
Gm.Drop: Drop an item (snare, poison) or a hazard here — or just enter a name and a DC.
Gm.Name: Name
Gm.Desc: Description (shown when it's sprung; @Check[reflex|dc:20] buttons work)
Gm.DescHint: e.g. The floor gives way onto spikes. @Check[reflex|dc:20|basic]; on a failure, 2d8 piercing.
Gm.CloseAsk: The players' trap time is still open. Close it along with this window?
Gm.CloseAskKeep: Keep it open, just close the window

Place.Hint: Click a square to place the trap (right-click / Esc: cancel)
Place.NoGrid: Traps need a scene with a grid.
Place.Taken: There is a trap on that square already.

Phase.Open: The GM opened trap-setting — set your traps in secret from the trap window.
Phase.GmOpen: Player trap-setting is open. Their traps don't show on your screen.

Pop.Title: Trap sprung — {name}
Pop.RearmHint: Undo — arm the trap again as if nothing happened

Settings.DcModeHint: A trap item's own DC is usually too weak against tougher foes. The level DC scales with the setter's level — PF2e: GM Core level DCs; D&D 5e: 8 + proficiency bonus + 3; other systems: 10 + half the level.
Settings.DcBest: The higher of item DC and level DC
Settings.DcBonusHint: Added to the level DC (default +2, since monsters are usually stronger than the party).
Settings.PhaseHint: On (default): players can set traps only while the GM has trap-setting open.
Settings.PcHitsHint: Who springs a trap set by the players. The players' side: characters a player owns, members of the party, PF2e's “party” alliance, friendly tokens.
Settings.Enemies: Anyone not on the players' side
Settings.GmHitsHint: Who springs a trap set by the GM. The players' side: characters a player owns, members of the party, PF2e's “party” alliance, friendly tokens.
Settings.PeekNoticeHint: On: a chat message is posted whenever the GM peeks at the players' traps.
Settings.MarkersHint: (Players) Show your party's traps on the map.

RPT.Passed: {name} walked over your trap “{trap}” — it didn't go off: GM traps catch {who} (setting “Who sets off GM traps”).
